question: Can the testing-esp32-duts single-layer A* kernel repair a layout-trace-style transactional via removal, and can its failure evidence distinguish a necessary layer excursion from a broken repair mechanism?

architecture.topology_edit: layout-trace-style atomic remove/merge across every occurrence of one physical via
architecture.transaction: remove first, reroute each newly merged maximal same-layer run, rebuild canonical segments/vias, then native-gate the full KiCad rung
architecture.current_limit: the repair adds no vias and searches one copper layer; a layer-changing repair is deliberately not misreported as via reduction

branch8_long_corridor_negative.direct_front_result: two vias removed, but the replacement chord produces 19 native DRC findings
branch8_long_corridor_negative.direct_back_result: one physical via removed, but the merged route produces 28 native DRC findings
branch8_long_corridor_negative.interpretation: expanding the window by 8 mm and refining to 0.125 mm still finds no zero-new-via same-layer path, so window clipping is not the main failure; this particular excursion is topologically useful under the present routing field

worked: the combined topology-edit/repair seam removes two real vias where either direct replacement chord is illegal
all three front-layer resolutions produce native-complete boards, proving the branch-8 failure is fixture-specific rather than a dead integration seam
the selected 0.25 mm action improves both canonical whole-tree length and via count
bounded search work and the exact native gate are retained per materialized action
surprises: the finest grid has the shortest local replacement path but not the shortest canonical whole-tree copper
the 0.25 mm path is selected because its geometry reuses the existing physical tree more effectively; local A* cost alone is not the correct multi-terminal objective
the coarse route is valid but makes the whole tree 12.366086 mm longer, so passing DRC is insufficient for action selection
did_not_establish: one successful private excursion does not imply arbitrary vias are removable
the current local search cannot add a compensating via pair, move components, or negotiate other nets
unsupported searches retain expansion counts in their detail but not yet a materialized diagnostic path/frontier overlay
CPU grid-search work is not a GPU performance result
critical_evaluation.next: make failed local searches retain structured grid/frontier evidence and a board overlay, then expose the action as one replaceable producer inside a broader topology search rather than scanning or deleting vias greedily
